name: kill
purpose: Terminate a running process using its Process ID (PID).
explanation: Sends a signal to a running process. By default, 'kill <PID>' sends SIGTERM (15), politely requesting the process to clean up and exit. 'kill -9 <PID>' sends SIGKILL (9), forcing immediate termination without cleanup.

parameters.description: Sends SIGKILL (signal 9) to force immediate termination without cleanup.

whenToUse: To stop a frozen or runaway process after finding its PID via ps, top, or htop.
commonMistakes: Passing the program name instead of its numeric PID.
Using kill -9 before trying a polite SIGTERM when cleanup matters.
explanationOfOutput: Shows the simulated terminal response when running `kill` in a standard Unix-like shell.
commonErrors: zsh: command not found: kill (if not installed or missing from PATH)
